# supervise

```go
import "github.com/lucasavila00/immutago/pkg/supervise"
```

Package supervise manages background services and restarts them after a panic.

Define a service:

- Embed Service\[A\] for start arguments of type A; use NoArgs for no arguments.
- Supply Run\(context.Context\) for background work.
- Declare Init\(\) error for setup, or use the default Init from Service\[A\].
- Start calls Init, returns Ref\[T\], and schedules Run in a managed goroutine.

Call a service:

- Keep the Ref and use ref.Current\(\).Method\(\).
- Calls run in the caller's goroutine and can overlap with Run and other calls. Synchronize access to mutable fields.
- Each exported service method returns no result or one service result: a scalar, a Ref, an im.ByValue struct or marker, or an unnamed array of these types. This includes promoted methods. Init, Run, and methods supplied by the runtime are exempt. See the complete result rules at https://github.com/lucasavila00/immutago/blob/main/docs/service-results.md.
- Arguments and implementation code follow ordinary Go rules. Uses of im values keep their immutability and pointer rules.

Service methods can give callbacks or globals access to mutable state. Review state changes, locks, saved inputs, and dependency calls in the service code.

### Groups and shutdown

- NewRoot creates an application group; StartGroup creates a nested group.
- Service.Children supplies the group for one run. Children created during Init wait for Run to begin.
- Group.Stop returns a completion channel. Children stop last started first, before their parent's Run context is cancelled.
- Run must return when its context ends. Stop cannot force it to return and does not wait for direct method calls. Init has no cancellation context.

### Replacement and failure

- Normal Run return ends the service. A panic starts a delayed restart.
- Delay starts at 1 second and doubles for each restart in the last 5 minutes.
- Each attempt creates a fresh value with the same arguments and calls Init. Successful setup replaces the current value; failed setup counts as a failure.
- Six failures from one child in 5 minutes stop its siblings and pass failure to the parent group. The parent restarts that group under the same rules. Failure at the root panics and ends the program.
- NewRoot can report recovered panics and restart Init errors before each delay.
- Current selects the last published value, even during delays and after stop. Calls in progress finish on their selected value.
- A direct call's panic stays in its goroutine. Calls from Run or a restart Init can fail that attempt. The first Init panic reaches the Start caller.
- A child Ref does not follow its parent's restart.

## func StartReserved

```go
func StartReserved[T, A any, P interface {
    *T
    Init() error
    Run(context.Context)
    bind(A, func(any, []byte))
    begin(context.Context) context.Context
    end()
}](parent *Group, ref Ref[T], args A) error
```

StartReserved starts a reference from Reserve under parent. It sets args on a fresh T and calls Init before publishing T or starting Run. An Init error leaves ref unstarted, so the caller can retry. An Init panic reaches the caller.

Each restart repeats setup on a fresh value with the same args. Failed setup keeps the previous value in ref. If parent has stopped, Init still runs but Run does not. The runtime stops children created by a value that will not run.

Starting an already started reference panics. If concurrent starts compete, the one that loses publication stops its staged children and panics.

## type ConcurrentSafe

ConcurrentSafe carries a caller's promise that its value is safe for concurrent use. The wrapper adds no synchronization and has no special checker rule. Ordinary service arguments can hold T directly.

```go

```

### func AssumeConcurrentSafe

```go
func AssumeConcurrentSafe[T any](v T) ConcurrentSafe[T]
```

AssumeConcurrentSafe records the caller's promise that concurrent use of v is safe. It adds no checking, synchronization, or immutability to v.

### func \(ConcurrentSafe\[T\]\) Value

```go
func (d ConcurrentSafe[T]) Value() T
```

Value reads the wrapped dependency. A zero ConcurrentSafe value contains the zero value of T.

## type Group

Group manages the lifetime and restart rules of its child services and groups. Create a root with NewRoot or a nested group with StartGroup. The zero value is not usable. A group returned by Service.Children belongs to that service run.

```go
type Group struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

### func NewRoot

```go
func NewRoot(report func(value any, stack []byte)) *Group
```

NewRoot creates a running root group. A failure that reaches this group panics and ends the program.

If report is non\-nil, it receives each recovered panic or restart Init error and a stack before the restart delay. Child groups use the same function. Reports for different children can overlap. The group waits for report to return, and a panic in report is not recovered. Do not wait for that group to stop inside report.

### func StartGroup

```go
func StartGroup(parent *Group) *Group
```

StartGroup creates a child group under parent. Use it to stop selected services together or restart them together when a child passes its restart limit. A stopped parent returns a stopped group. When this group's Stop channel closes, the parent has also removed it from the child list.

### func \(\*Group\) Stop

```go
func (s *Group) Stop() <-chan struct{}
```

Stop requests shutdown and returns its completion channel without waiting. Repeated calls return the same channel. The channel closes after all children stop, last started first, and a nested group is removed from its parent.

Run methods must return when their contexts end. Stop does not wait for direct service method calls, and their references remain callable. A Run method can request its own group's stop, but must not wait for that stop to complete.

## type NoArgs

NoArgs supplies an empty start argument. Embed Service\[NoArgs\] and pass NoArgs\{\} to Start when the service needs no arguments.

```go
type NoArgs struct{}
```

## type Ref

Ref is a reference to one service. Copies select the same service, including after a restart. The analyzer requires T to be a concrete struct that embeds Service. References can be stored in immutable fields and returned as service results; the service state can still change. Start returns an initialized reference. Reserve creates one for later startup; a zero Ref is empty and cannot be used in place of Reserve.

```go
type Ref[T any] struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

### func Reserve

```go
func Reserve[T any]() Ref[T]
```

Reserve creates a reference that StartReserved can initialize later. Use it to connect services whose start arguments need each other's references. Current panics until initialization succeeds.

### func Start

```go
func Start[T, A any, P interface {
    *T
    Init() error
    Run(context.Context)
    bind(A, func(any, []byte))
    begin(context.Context) context.Context
    end()
}](parent *Group, args A) (Ref[T], error)
```

Start creates T with args, calls Init, and returns its reference after setup succeeds. Run then runs under parent. Only T must be written as a type argument.

An Init error returns an empty Ref and that error. An Init panic reaches the caller. If parent has stopped, setup still runs but Run does not. Start uses Reserve and StartReserved; their initialization and restart rules apply.

### func \(Ref\[T\]\) Current

```go
func (p Ref[T]) Current() *T
```

Current selects the last successfully initialized service value with one atomic load. The analyzer accepts only ref.Current\(\).Method\(args\). Method must be an exported service method other than Init, Run, or a runtime method. The analyzer rejects saving the pointer, the Current method, or the selected method. A call in progress finishes on its selected instance, even after a restart.

Current panics for an empty or unstarted reference. It can select a value whose Run has ended. Stop does not invalidate the reference or block later calls.

## type Service

Service supplies the arguments and child group of a supervised service. Embed Service\[A\] to supply start arguments and runtime methods; add Run\(context.Context\) for background work. Start and StartReserved create and initialize each service value. Call an exported service method with ref.Current\(\).Method\(args\).

```go
type Service[A any] struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

### func \(\*Service\[A\]\) Args

```go
func (p *Service[A]) Args() A
```

Args reads the start arguments of this service value. Each restart receives the same arguments.

### func \(\*Service\[A\]\) Children

```go
func (p *Service[A]) Children() *Group
```

Children returns the group owned by this service run. Use it as the parent of Start, StartReserved, or StartGroup. The runtime stops it when this run ends. To stop selected children separately, create a nested group.

Each run has a separate child group. Children created before Run begins wait for that run. Failed setup stops them without running them. On stop, the runtime waits for children, last started first, before it cancels this service's Run context. A return or panic from Run also stops the children before the run ends.

A child that passes its restart limit fails this run. After the run ends, Children returns a stopped group; later starts can initialize but cannot run.

### func \(\*Service\[A\]\) Init

```go
func (*Service[A]) Init() error
```

Init supplies successful empty setup when the service does not declare Init. The runtime calls Init on each fresh value before Current or Run can use it. A declared Init must release any application resources it opened before returning an error; the runtime stops staged children.
